market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: CEE Banks Prepare for Implementation
market.summary_short: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation is set to transform payment processing across Europe, requiring banks to offer instant credit transfers at no extra cost. CEE banks are actively preparing for the upcoming deadlines, focusing on technical upgrades and compliance.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's new Instant Payments Regulation, which entered into force in April 2024, mandates that all EU/EEA banks must offer instant credit transfers in EUR within 10 seconds, 24/7/365, at the same or lower cost as standard SEPA credit transfers. The first deadline for receiving instant payments is January 2025 for Eurozone banks, with sending capabilities required by October 2025. Non-Eurozone banks have slightly later deadlines, extending into 2026 and 2027. This regulation aims to accelerate the adoption of instant payments, enhance liquidity management for corporates, and foster innovation. CEE banks, including those in the RBI network, are heavily investing in infrastructure upgrades and compliance frameworks to meet these stringent requirements, impacting their core banking systems and customer-facing platforms.
key_points: EU Instant Payments Regulation mandates 10-second EUR transfers.
No extra cost for instant payments compared to standard SEPA.
Eurozone banks' first deadline for receiving is January 2025.
Non-Eurozone banks face deadlines extending into 2026/2027.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for RBI Cash Management and CMIplus, driving demand for real-time payment processing capabilities across CEE. CMIplus must ensure full compliance and offer seamless instant payment initiation and reception, leveraging its multi-currency and multi-country infrastructure to support corporate clients' liquidity needs.

market.summary_detail: The demand for sophisticated treasury technology is surging among German and European corporates. Companies are moving beyond basic functionalities, seeking TMS solutions that offer deep integration with ERP systems, payment factories, and banking channels like EBICS and H2H. The focus is on end-to-end automation of payment initiation, reconciliation, and liquidity forecasting. The ongoing migration to ISO 20022 for cross-border and domestic payments further necessitates robust system capabilities for handling richer data formats. Treasurers aim to reduce manual efforts, minimize operational risks, and gain a consolidated, real-time view of their global cash positions, especially crucial for multi-entity and multi-currency operations common in CEE.

Focus on end-to-end automation for payments and reconciliation.

market.title: Fighting Payment Fraud: VoP Solutions Gain Traction in Europe
market.summary_short: Payment fraud remains a significant threat to corporates, prompting increased adoption of advanced fraud prevention technologies, particularly Confirmation of Payee (CoP) or Validation of Payee (VoP) solutions. These tools are gaining traction across Europe to combat authorized push payment (APP) fraud.
market.summary_detail: European corporates are facing a rising tide of payment fraud, including invoice fraud, CEO fraud, and authorized push payment (APP) fraud, where victims are tricked into sending money to fraudsters. In response, banks and fintechs are rolling out Validation of Payee (VoP) services, similar to the UK's Confirmation of Payee (CoP). These services allow payers to verify the recipient's name against their bank account details before initiating a payment, significantly reducing the risk of misdirected funds. While not yet mandated across the entire EU, several countries are exploring or implementing such schemes. The upcoming PSD3 directive is expected to further emphasize fraud prevention measures, potentially accelerating VoP adoption and integration into corporate payment workflows, especially for high-value and cross-border transactions.
key_points: Payment fraud, especially APP fraud, is a growing concern.
Validation of Payee (VoP) verifies recipient details before payment.
VoP reduces misdirected funds and APP fraud risks.
PSD3 expected to boost VoP adoption across Europe.
market.rbi_cash_management: For CMIplus, integrating VoP capabilities is crucial for enhancing security and trust for corporate clients. Offering robust fraud prevention tools, potentially via Open Banking APIs or direct integration, will differentiate RBI's cash management services and protect clients from financial losses, particularly important in the CEE region where fraud tactics evolve.

market.title: EU Mandates Instant Payments: ISO 20022 Critical for Compliance
market.summary_short: The European Union has finalized legislation requiring all SEPA credit transfers to be processed instantly by early 2027, with full compliance expected across the Eurozone and non-Eurozone SEPA countries. This regulation also mandates that instant payments must be offered at no additional cost compared to standard transfers, significantly impacting banking infrastructure and corporate treasury operations.
market.summary_detail: The new EU Instant Payments Regulation, officially adopted, sets a clear timeline for banks to enable instant credit transfers for all customers. Eurozone banks must be ready to receive instant payments by early 2027 and send them by mid-2027, with non-Eurozone SEPA countries following shortly after. A key component of this mandate is the universal adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging standard, which provides richer data capabilities essential for real-time processing and reconciliation. Banks are also required to implement robust fraud prevention measures and offer a "Verification of Payee" (VoP) service to mitigate risks associated with faster payments. This regulatory push aims to modernize the European payment landscape, fostering innovation and improving liquidity management for corporates.
key_points: EU Instant Payments Regulation finalized.
Mandatory instant payments by early 2027 for Eurozone.
ISO 20022 messaging standard is compulsory.
Verification of Payee (VoP) service required.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Strengthen Payment Security and Fraud Prevention
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposed PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation (PSR) aim to significantly enhance payment security and combat fraud across the EU. These new regulations will introduce stricter requirements for payment service providers, including mandatory fraud reporting and improved data sharing mechanisms.
market.summary_detail: Building on the foundations of PSD2, the upcoming PSD3 and PSR package seeks to address emerging fraud patterns, particularly those associated with instant payments and authorized push payment (APP) fraud. Key proposals include extending the scope of strong customer authentication (SCA) to more transaction types, mandating the implementation of robust fraud detection and prevention tools, and improving information sharing between banks and payment service providers to identify and mitigate threats more effectively. The regulations also emphasize consumer protection, aiming to increase the recovery rates for fraud victims. For corporate treasuries, this means a heightened focus on internal controls, enhanced security protocols for payment initiation, and closer collaboration with banking partners to ensure compliance and safeguard against financial crime.
key_points: PSD3/PSR proposals target payment fraud.
Extends Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) scope.
Mandates robust fraud detection and prevention tools.
Aims to improve information sharing among providers.

The overarching goal is to foster competition and innovation in the digital payments landscape while ensuring a high level of consumer trust and security across the EU and CEE.

regulatory.title: EBA Highlights VOP Matching Challenges for Instant Payments
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group released a note detailing key pain points impacting the accuracy of VOP matching checks. These challenges include the lack of standardised name-matching logic and limitations related to name field length and virtual accounts.
regulatory.summary_detail: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group (IPG) has published an insight note addressing critical challenges in implementing Verification of Payee (VoP) matching checks. VoP is a crucial fraud prevention measure, especially for instant payments, and its accuracy is paramount for compliance and customer trust. The note identifies several pain points, such as the absence of a standardised name-matching logic across different systems and jurisdictions, restrictions on name field lengths in payment messages, and specific limitations when dealing with virtual accounts. These issues can lead to false positives or negatives, impacting the efficiency and reliability of VoP, and require careful consideration by PSPs for effective implementation under the Instant Payments Regulation.
key_points: VoP matching accuracy is critical for instant payments and fraud prevention.
Lack of standardised name-matching logic creates implementation pain points.
Name field length restrictions impact VoP check quality.
